answer: In an agent marketplace handling tundra surveys, canyon mapping, and juniper inventories, each bidding identity must lock a $1,000 bond for 90 days before accepting work. Selection weight is proportional to bonded capital, not account count, so splitting funds among aliases buys no extra influence. Creating 100 eligible fake agents ties up $100,000: the attacker must supply real capital and forgo its use elsewhere throughout the lockup.
